questions.question: Across the four dedicated heart failure outcome trials of SGLT2 inhibitors (DAPA-HF, EMPEROR-Reduced, EMPEROR-Preserved, DELIVER), how large was the reduction in the primary composite outcome in each, and does the effect hold across the ejection fraction range?

keyPoints.text: DAPA-HF (ejection fraction 40% or less): dapagliflozin reduced worsening heart failure or cardiovascular death, hazard ratio 0.74 (16.3% vs 21.2%).

support.quote: the primary outcome occurred in 386 of 2373 patients (16.3%) in the dapagliflozin group and in 502 of 2371 patients (21.2%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.74; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.65 to 0.85; P<0.001)

keyPoints.text: EMPEROR-Reduced (ejection fraction 40% or less): empagliflozin reduced cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization, hazard ratio 0.75 (19.4% vs 24.7%).

support.quote: a primary outcome event occurred in 361 of 1863 patients (19.4%) in the empagliflozin group and in 462 of 1867 patients (24.7%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio for cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure, 0.75; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.65 to 0.86; P<0.001)

keyPoints.text: EMPEROR-Preserved (ejection fraction above 40%): empagliflozin reduced the primary outcome, hazard ratio 0.79 (13.8% vs 17.1%).

support.quote: a primary outcome event occurred in 415 of 2997 patients (13.8%) in the empagliflozin group and in 511 of 2991 patients (17.1%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.79; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.69 to 0.90; P<0.001)

keyPoints.text: DELIVER (mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction, above 40%): dapagliflozin reduced the primary outcome, hazard ratio 0.82 (16.4% vs 19.5%); results were similar for ejection fraction of 60% or more and less than 60%.

support.quote: the primary outcome occurred in 512 of 3131 patients (16.4%) in the dapagliflozin group and in 610 of 3132 patients (19.5%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.82; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.73 to 0.92; P<0.001)
Results were similar among patients with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 60% or more and those with a left ventricular ejection fraction of less than 60%

questions.question: Did SGLT2 inhibitors reduce cardiovascular death on its own, as opposed to hospitalization for heart failure? Compare DAPA-HF, DELIVER, EMPEROR-Preserved and what the heart failure meta-analysis concluded.

keyPoints.text: DAPA-HF: death from cardiovascular causes was significantly lower with dapagliflozin (hazard ratio 0.82; 95% CI 0.69 to 0.98).

support.quote: Death from cardiovascular causes occurred in 227 patients (9.6%) in the dapagliflozin group and in 273 patients (11.5%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.69 to 0.98)

keyPoints.text: DELIVER: cardiovascular death alone was not significantly reduced (hazard ratio 0.88; 95% CI 0.74 to 1.05), while worsening heart failure was (hazard ratio 0.79).

support.quote: cardiovascular death occurred in 231 patients (7.4%) and 261 patients (8.3%), respectively (hazard ratio, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.74 to 1.05)

keyPoints.text: EMPEROR-Preserved: the effect on the primary outcome was mainly related to a lower risk of hospitalization for heart failure.

support.quote: This effect was mainly related to a lower risk of hospitalization for heart failure in the empagliflozin group.

keyPoints.text: The meta-analysis of five trials concluded that SGLT2 inhibitors reduced cardiovascular death (hazard ratio 0.87; 95% CI 0.79 to 0.95) and first hospitalisation for heart failure (0.72); in DELIVER plus EMPEROR-Preserved alone cardiovascular death was 0.88 (0.77 to 1.00).

questions.question: How did the populations of the three chronic kidney disease trials (CREDENCE, DAPA-CKD, EMPA-KIDNEY) differ in kidney function, albuminuria and diabetes status, and was the effect consistent with and without diabetes?

keyPoints.text: CREDENCE enrolled only patients with type 2 diabetes and albuminuric chronic kidney disease (eGFR 30 to <90, albumin-to-creatinine ratio >300 to 5000) on renin-angiotensin system blockade; it tested canagliflozin 100 mg daily.

support.quote: we assigned patients with type 2 diabetes and albuminuric chronic kidney disease to receive canagliflozin, an oral SGLT2 inhibitor, at a dose of 100 mg daily or placebo
estimated glomerular filtration rate (GFR) of 30 to <90 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area and albuminuria (ratio of albumin [mg] to creatinine [g], >300 to 5000)

keyPoints.text: DAPA-CKD enrolled participants with an eGFR of 25 to 75 and a urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio of 200 to 5000, with or without type 2 diabetes; the effects were similar in those with and without diabetes.

support.quote: estimated glomerular filtration rate (GFR) of 25 to 75 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area and a urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (with albumin measured in milligrams and creatinine measured in grams) of 200 to 5000
The effects of dapagliflozin were similar in participants with type 2 diabetes and in those without type 2 diabetes.

keyPoints.text: EMPA-KIDNEY was the broadest: eGFR of at least 20 but under 45, or eGFR of at least 45 but under 90 with an albumin-to-creatinine ratio of at least 200; results were consistent with or without diabetes and across eGFR ranges.

support.quote: estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of at least 20 but less than 45 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area, or who had an eGFR of at least 45 but less than 90 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 with a urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio
Results were consistent among patients with or without diabetes and across subgroups defined according to eGFR ranges.

keyPoints.text: EMPA-KIDNEY: no significant between-group difference in death from any cause (4.5% vs 5.1%).
